questions.question: A four-shard service receives 120,000 writes per second. One shard receives 48% of them. How many writes per second reach that shard?
questions.explanation: Multiply total demand by the hot shard's share: 120,000 x 0.48 = 57,600 writes per second. The balanced average of 30,000 would hide this pressure.

questions.question: Which invariant is most important while moving a logical shard to a new physical owner?
options: Every shard always has the same row count
One authoritative owner exists for each routing epoch and acknowledged writes remain reachable
Both owners accept writes until traffic naturally moves
questions.explanation: Versioned single ownership prevents split-brain writes, while snapshot plus ordered catch-up preserves acknowledged changes through the move.

questions.question: Why can hashing by order_id be a poor shard key for a tenant dashboard even when write load is balanced?
options: One tenant's records can span all shards, forcing fanout and result merging
It always creates a global transaction
questions.explanation: Order hashing improves distribution but removes tenant locality. A tenant-scoped query may contact and merge data from every owner.

questions.question: For N = 5 replicas, which R and W pair guarantees read/write quorum overlap?
questions.explanation: Read/write overlap requires R + W > N. Only 3 + 3 = 6 is greater than 5 among these choices.

questions.question: With N = 5 and W = 3, how many replica failures can occur before that write quorum becomes impossible?
questions.explanation: The failure budget is N - W = 5 - 3 = 2. Three live replicas can still acknowledge the write after two failures.

questions.question: A user must immediately see an item they just added to a cart, while other users may briefly see older state. Which model fits best?
options: Eventual consistency with no session tracking
A stale replica chosen at random
questions.explanation: Session consistency can preserve the user's own write history without requiring every observer to see the newest value immediately.

questions.question: Why is a live replica not a substitute for an independent backup?
options: Replication can quickly copy deletion or corruption to every replica
A replica cannot use a write-ahead log
questions.explanation: Replication preserves availability against machine loss, but logical damage can propagate. Independent point-in-time recovery protects a different failure class.

questions.question: After cutover to routing epoch 42, a stale client sends a write with epoch 41 to the old owner. What should happen?
options: Accept the write and copy it later
Reject the stale epoch or return a moved response, then retry with the same operation identity
questions.explanation: Fencing prevents two authoritative writers. The client refreshes routing and retries idempotently against the current owner.
